content: Each project has a project_uid (UUID) in the SQLite registry, written into .claude-memory/manifest.json as `project_id`. Because that file is committed, moving or renaming a project folder re-binds the existing project instead of registering a duplicate, and a teammate's clone resolves to the same project. Resolution order in ProjectService.claim_folder: uid match (matched/rebound) -> same-slug project bound to this same folder or with no uid (adopted) -> otherwise a new project on a free slug (created). detect_project_from_cwd checks the manifest uid first, then falls back to portable DB / bound path / folder name. The sync CLI calls POST /api/hook/claim before import or export, and session-start.sh runs `sync import` BEFORE auto-register so auto-register can never create the duplicate first.

content:
Decided 2026-09-03. memory-mcp is gaining a task concept. Key constraints agreed with the user:

1. memory-mcp MUST work fully without asoode. Some users won't run a PM app. So the local `tasks` tables in per-project DuckDB are a complete working task store (create, describe, assign, state, comments, time tracking) — NOT a thin ledger.
2. asoode integration is per-project, OPT-IN, and fully configurable. asoode is on-premise, so base_url / socket_url / project id / work package id are all per-link config. Never hardcode a host. Copy the gateway rule from project_service.py:66-67 — a project is never auto-bound, so private projects can't leak.
3. The asoode PAT is stored in app_settings['cred:<base_url>'] (registry.py:238-252), keyed by URL not project, and never enters the committable .claude-memory/ snapshot.
4. Offline-first: every mirrorable mutation appends to a `task_outbox` row and returns immediately. Connection loss is a normal state. On reconnect: drain outbox in order per task, then reconcile inbound.
5. Inbound uses a LIVE Socket.IO subscription (user's choice over polling), from a new asyncio task in daemon.build_app()'s lifespan. No such background mechanism exists today. This makes asoode's socket authentication a hard blocker. A reconcile poll runs on every reconnect since socket delivery is not durable.
6. Tasks live in DuckDB and NEVER enter the JSON snapshot. This is what kills the user's "JSON files could become 100MB+" worry. WARNING: SYNC_CATEGORIES is derived automatically (constants.py:24), so tasks must be separate TABLES, not a memory category — otherwise they start being written to .claude-memory/.
7. One claude project -> many asoode work packages is solved by a `project_links` table in the SQLite registry with a `match_paths` JSON column: in a monorepo, apps/backend/** routes to the backend board, apps/frontend/** to the frontend board.

Rejected: building a full task manager UI in memory-mcp to replace asoode (duplicates a product the user already owns, and memory-mcp is a single-Mac launchd daemon with no phone access and no team model). Also rejected: a pure bridge with no local storage (asoode has no externalRef field, so without local state every retry duplicates).

DuckDB-vs-JSON exchange question answered: neither — don't move files. DuckDB stays the local store, the wire is small incremental JSON over HTTP. Measured: a DuckDB file with ONE row is 5.26 MB (block allocation + persisted HNSW dominate, files never shrink); JSON snapshots are 22-650x smaller.

Full docs in docs/bridge/ (01 asoode analysis, 02 memory-mcp analysis, 03 Claude UI surfaces, 04 design decisions).
summary: Tasks module + optional asoode bridge: local-first, offline-tolerant: Decided 2026-09-03
title: Tasks module + optional asoode bridge: local-first, offline-tolerant

content: frontend/src/components/TaskListView.tsx follows asoode's WpListView.tsx and TaskDialog.tsx follows its TaskModal/TaskModalMain/TaskModalSidebar. Both apps use the same shadcn design tokens, so the classes ported almost verbatim. asoode groups a list by board column; this store has no columns, so the STATE is the group - which is why the group pill is painted with the state colour and the inline add row inside a group creates a task already in that state. State and priority colours in lib/tasks.ts are asoode's exact hex values so the two apps read the same way side by side. Within a state, `position` outranks priority in the sort - otherwise dragging a task past a higher-priority one would silently snap back. The task dialog sits at z-40, BELOW the app's Dialog layer (z-50) and toasts (z-100), so a confirm opened from inside it lands on top.
summary: The Tasks UI is a port of asoode's list mode and task modal: frontend/src/components/TaskListView
title: The Tasks UI is a port of asoode's list mode and task modal

content: Schema v5 adds tasks / task_comments / task_time_entries to the per-project DuckDB, plus sessions.last_seen_at. They are deliberately NOT a MemoryCategory: SYNC_CATEGORIES is derived automatically from the category enum (constants.py:24), so a task category would immediately start writing every task into the committed .claude-memory/*.json snapshot. Keeping them in their own tables is the whole reason the "JSON grows to 100MB" problem cannot happen. TestTasksStayOutOfTheSnapshot asserts it. The state vocabulary is asoode's WorkPackageTaskState verbatim (todo/in_progress/done/paused/blocked/cancelled/duplicate/incomplete/blocker) so the Phase 2 bridge maps names to ordinals losslessly. task_time_entries uses begin_at/end_at rather than begin/end because `end` is a DuckDB reserved word that cannot be used as a column name even in a plain SELECT.

title: Tasks are separate DuckDB tables, never a MemoryCategory
